name: TextMateSharp
description: C# TextMate grammar engine port (from tm4e/vscode-textmate); used by AvaloniaEdit

host-language.comment: A .NET (C#) port of vscode-textmate, based on the Java port Eclipse tm4e. Targets netstandard2.0.

form-factor.comment: NuGet library (TextMateSharp, plus the TextMateSharp.Grammars package for bundled grammars and themes). The repo has a console demo project but no shipped CLI.

license.comment: TextMateSharp and TextMateSharp.Grammars are both MIT on NuGet. The NuGet page has no separate note on licences for the bundled grammars and themes.

documentation.comment: No docs site. The README has install steps, one usage example and a pointer to the demo project.

first-release.comment: Repo created 2021-06-23. NuGet 1.0.0 shows a last-updated date of 2021-06-28.

latest-version.comment: Latest stable version as of 2026-11-19, released 2026-11-03. 3.0.0-preview.1 (managed GregsEx regex engine) came out the same day as a prerelease.

engine-model.comment: Interprets TextMate grammars. It is a port of vscode-textmate by way of tm4e.

regex-engine.comment: Stable 1.x/2.x use Onigwrap, a native wrapper around the C Oniguruma library. 3.0.0-preview.1 (2026-11-03) replaces it with GregsEx, a fully managed C# implementation of Oniguruma 6.9.10. Its release notes say tokens are byte-identical to Onigwrap's on the samples for all bundled grammars. Once 3.0 is stable, this would become `custom`.

embedded-languages.comment: The bundled HTML grammar pulls in `source.js` and `source.css` with `include`, and RegistryOptions.GetGrammar resolves bundled grammars by scope name, so HTML+JS+CSS works without extra setup. Cross-grammar injections are not supported (per the README, and `GetInjections` always returns null), so injection-based embedding does not work. Judged from the code; no published output example was checked.

language-auto-detection.comment: No content-based detection. Grammars are looked up by scope, language id or file extension.

filename-extension-mapping.comment: RegistryOptions has `GetLanguageByExtension` and `GetScopeByExtension`. These use the `contributes.languages` data in each bundled grammar's package.json.

resumable-line-state.comment: `TokenizeLine(lineText, prevState, timeLimit)` returns a `RuleStack` (IStateStack) that is passed in for the next line. A time limit allows time-sliced tokenization.

incremental-reparsing.comment: No edit-aware reparse. After an edit, callers re-tokenize from the changed line using the stored per-line state stacks.

semantic-distinctions.comment: Pure TextMate regex state machine with no syntax tree, so `false` per the guideline.

bundled-languages.comment: Counted the 51 entries in GrammarNames.SupportedGrammars on master, as of 2026-11-19. Each entry is a VS Code-style grammar package, e.g. Asciidoc, C#, C++, HTML, Python, Rust, Typst, YAML. Some packages hold several grammars (Git, Cpp, Markdown), and the 3.0.0-preview.1 notes count 63 grammars. The README says "50+ languages".

grammar-format.comment: The README says grammars load from JSON only. Plist .tmLanguage is not supported.

grammar-ecosystem-compatibility.comment: Consumes VS Code extension grammar packages (package.json with `contributes.grammars` and JSON grammars) directly. Limits: no cross-grammar injections and no plist grammars.

runtime-grammar-loading.comment: `RegistryOptions.LoadFromLocalDir` / `LoadFromLocalFile` register VS Code-style grammar packages from disk at runtime, with optional overwrite. A custom IRegistryOptions can also supply grammars.

lazy-grammar-loading.comment: Grammar and theme files are read only when `GetGrammar` / `GetTheme` is called. Each bundled package's package.json metadata is parsed when RegistryOptions is constructed.

grammar-accuracy.comment: The bundled grammars are VS Code extension grammars, and since 3.0.0-preview.1 vscode-textmate's tokenization test suites run in CI. Rated 4 rather than 5 because cross-grammar injections are not supported, so grammars that depend on injections (such as the Markdown math injection) can fall short of VS Code. How often the grammars are re-synced with VS Code was not verified.

bundled-themes.comment: Counted 21 ThemeName values mapped in RegistryOptions.GetThemeFile on master, as of 2026-11-19, matching the 21 files in Resources/Themes. They include Dark+/Light+, Dark/Light (VS), Monokai, Dimmed Monokai, One Dark, Atom One Light/Dark, Dracula, Solarized Dark/Light, both High Contrast themes, Visual Studio Dark/Light, Abyss, Kimbie Dark, Quiet Light, Red and Tomorrow Night Blue. The README says 22.

theme-format.comment: The bundled themes are VS Code colour-theme JSON files, e.g. dark_plus.json and monokai-color-theme.json.

token-classification.comment: Each IToken has a list of hierarchical TextMate scope names.

css-class-output.comment: No rendering of any kind. The API returns tokens only.

multi-theme-output.comment: One theme per Registry. Since there is no rendered output, nothing can serve several themes from one pass. Callers can re-match the scope tokens against another theme themselves.

public-token-api.comment: Tokens are the library's only output. The public `IGrammar.TokenizeLine` / `TokenizeLine2` methods are shown in the README example.

ir-kinds.comment: `TokenizeLine` returns IToken {StartIndex, EndIndex, Length, Scopes}, a scope stack per token. `TokenizeLine2` returns an `int[] Tokens` array of encoded offset/metadata pairs, the binary styled-span form ported from vscode-textmate.

serializable-ir.comment: Tokens are plain objects or an int array, but no serialization is documented. The state stack is an in-memory object.

theme-resolved-tokens.comment: The documented path is `theme.Match(token.Scopes)`, which returns rules with foreground/background colour ids and font style, then `theme.GetColor(id)` for the hex colour (as in the README and the demo). `TokenizeLine2` metadata also encodes these attributes, following vscode-textmate.

source-offsets-in-ir.comment: Tokens carry StartIndex/EndIndex character offsets within the line. The caller tracks line numbers.

custom-formatter-api.comment: No formatter or renderer abstraction. Callers render the tokens themselves (the demo uses Spectre.Console), but there is no documented extension point for this.

output-formats.comment: No first-party output formats. It emits tokens only. The demo renders to the terminal via the third-party Spectre.Console, and AvaloniaEdit.TextMate renders into an editor control.

line-numbers.comment: No rendered output, so no line numbers.

streaming-output.comment: The API works strictly one line at a time: `TokenizeLine(line, prevState, ...)` returns tokens for each line without needing the rest of the input. The output is tokens, not rendered text.

terminal-ready.comment: No ANSI output in the library. The demo shows terminal output built with Spectre.Console.

native-dependencies.comment: Stable 2.0.5 depends on Onigwrap (>= 1.0.11), which wraps the native Oniguruma C library (libonigwrap). 3.0.0-preview.1 removes all native dependencies by switching to the managed GregsEx engine, so this becomes `none` once 3.0 is stable.

runs-in-browser.comment: Runs in .NET WebAssembly (Blazor-style) apps. 1.x/2.x need the TextMateSharp.Wasm package, which supplies the assets needed to build and run TextMateSharp on WASM (last updated 2024-07-31). 3.0.0-preview.1 runs on WebAssembly without it and adds a browser WasmDemo.

wasm-build.comment: WebAssembly is officially supported via the TextMateSharp.Wasm assets package for 1.x/2.x, and natively from 3.0 because the code is fully managed. It runs in the .NET WASM runtime rather than as a standalone .wasm module.

synchronous-api.comment: Registry setup, `LoadGrammar` and `TokenizeLine` are all synchronous.

bindings-ports.comment: No bindings for other languages. TextMateSharp is itself a C# port of vscode-textmate (JS) by way of Eclipse tm4e (Java).

core-package-size.comment: Size of the TextMateSharp 2.0.5 nupkg download (105.4 KB) as shown on NuGet on 2026-11-19, which is a compressed package rather than the installed size. Not included: the required Onigwrap native package (about 4 MB nupkg with native binaries) and the optional TextMateSharp.Grammars package (878 KB) with the bundled grammars and themes.

throughput-tier.comment: The only benchmark is the maintainers' 2.x vs 3.0 comparison: a 133k-line C# file tokenizes in about 5.1 s on Onigwrap and about 1.0 s on GregsEx (.NET 10, Apple M4 Pro). It includes no other highlighters, so no tier can be assigned under the guideline.

initialization-cost.comment: Not measured. RegistryOptions construction parses package.json metadata for all 51 bundled grammar packages, and grammars compile when first used. No published timing was found.

monthly-downloads.comment: Rough estimate from NuGet, as of 2026-11-19, since NuGet does not publish monthly counts. Version 2.0.4 (2026-06-04 to 2026-11-03) has about 505K downloads, or about 100K/month, and 2.0.3 (Feb to Jun 2026) has about 452K, or about 113K/month. The lifetime average is about 2.3K/day (about 2.0M total). Much of this traffic comes transitively through Terminal.Gui and AvaloniaEdit.TextMate.

last-release.comment: v2.0.5 stable, released the same day as the v3.0.0-preview.1 prerelease.

maintenance-status.comment: Regular releases: 2.0.0 to 2.0.5 between Dec 2025 and Nov 2026, plus the 3.0 preview. Last push 2026-11-13. The 2.x line is maintained on the release/2.x branch.

documentation-quality.comment: README with install steps, one usage example and a demo project. No API reference, guides or docs site.

notable-users.comment: NuGet's "Used by" list shows Terminal.Gui and AvaloniaEdit.TextMate as dependent packages, and AvaloniaUI/AvaloniaEdit, tui-cs/Terminal.Gui and IvanJosipovic/KubeUI among dependent GitHub repos (2026-11-19). The README names AvaloniaEdit.

bus-factor.comment: Lives in a personal repo. danipen has 453 of about 610 commits. Other notable contributors are udlose (62) and sebastienros (30, the GregsEx migration).
